classification.difficultyReason: Reframe six unknown shaded angles as three straight angles minus the inner triangle's angle sum, avoiding attempts to calculate individual angles.

content.prompt: Find the sum of all six angles shaded in the figure below.

spec.description: Outer triangle with an inner triangle meeting all three sides; the six angles outside the inner triangle are shaded.
spec.mathematics: At each inner vertex, two shaded angles and one inner-triangle angle form a straight angle.
spec.answerVisibility: No answers or invented vertex labels are visible.

answer.short:
$360^\circ$.

Subtract the inner triangle's angle sum from three straight angles.
answer.worked:
Let the inner triangle's angles be $x$, $y$ and $z$, and let $S$ be the sum of the shaded angles. Each inner vertex lies on a straight side of the outer triangle.

$$\begin{align*}x+y+z&=180^\circ\\S&=3\times180^\circ-(x+y+z)\\S&=540^\circ-180^\circ\\S&=360^\circ.\end{align*}$$
